_what: Phrases and constructions the creator has explicitly rejected, with the date and the reason. scripts/spoken_lint.py reads this file and FAILS any script that reproduces one. Copy this to <workspace>/voice-corpus/rejections.json and empty the array before first use: the entries below are illustrations of the SHAPE of a good entry, not rules for your creator.
_why: This is the only mechanism that accumulates the creator's taste across sessions. A model's weights do not change between runs and nothing about a conversation survives it, so a correction made today is lost tomorrow unless it lands in a file that executes. Prose guidance was tried first and failed: a 187-line document describing the voice in adjectives still produced pastiche, because a description of a voice generates an imitation of the description. A ledger of concrete rejected strings cannot be misread.
_how_to_add: When the creator kills a line, append it with the date and their reason, in their words where they gave them. NEVER add a phrase on your own judgement: this file is a record of their rulings, not a style opinion. Keep `pattern` a lowercase substring, or a regex flagged with is_regex, and keep it narrow enough that it cannot fire on legitimate copy.

rejections.why: EXAMPLE ENTRY. Domain shorthand compressing 'another earnings beat'. The creator's words: 'it just sounds weird. It's not something that I would ever say, nor do I know how to say it.' Jargon standing in for plain words: reads as clever on a page and is unsayable aloud.

rejections.pattern: (you'd think|you'd assume|you'd guess|everyone says|everyone assumes)[^.!?]{0,80}(and it is|and they do|and it was|and for years|and honestly)
rejections.why: EXAMPLE ENTRY. The ritual concede-then-pivot seam. It shipped 8 times in one batch because the show skeleton's 'assumption' beat was being satisfied by a formula instead of by a real surprise.

EXAMPLE ENTRY. The two-sentence antithesis epigram. Carries no fact and tells the viewer what to conclude. Clusters at the END of scripts, where it does most damage, because the symmetry sounds like a verdict.
